# Lead

`sales.obj.core.lead` · v1.0.0 · **draft** · scope **core**

> A Contact plus the evidence that they might be in market. Two discriminators, and both are load-bearing. Against Contact: intent evidence — without an observed act suggesting a reason to buy, you have a person, not a lead. Against Opportunity: no purchase process exists yet — no scoped need, no named money, no agreed next step with someone who could say yes. Most CRM hygiene disasters come from blurring one of those two boundaries. Blur the first and a purchased list becomes ten thousand leads, the top of the funnel inflates and conversion rate becomes meaningless. Blur the second and a warm conversation becomes forecast revenue. A lead is also temporary in a way a Contact is not: the same person can be a lead three times in five years, and each time is a separate claim with its own evidence and its own expiry.


Also called: `Prospect`, `Inquiry`, `MQL`, `SQL`

## Constraints

- **`lead.intent_required`** A Lead cannot exist with zero intent signals.
- **`lead.process_required`** Cannot convert to an Opportunity without a scoped need andan agreed next step with a named buyer.
- **`lead.reason_required`** Cannot be disqualified without disqualify_reason.
- **`lead.one_owner`** Exactly one owner_rep at a time.
- **`lead.contact_rules_apply`** Every Contact consent and do-not-contact constraint appliesunchanged. Intent is not permission.
- **`lead.pending_is_time_boxed`** A verdict of pending past its window is escalated ratherthan left. _(soft)_


## Business rules

- **`lead.no_lead_without_intent`** A Contact with no intent evidence may not be created as a Lead. A list import is a contact import. This is the rule the object exists to hold, and the one every quarterly pipeline target quietly pressures a team into breaking.

- **`lead.no_conversion_without_a_process`** A Lead may not convert to an Opportunity until a scoped need and an agreed next step with a named buyer both exist. Enthusiasm, a good meeting and a request for a proposal are none of those things.

- **`lead.disqualifier_beats_intent`** A lead matching any ICP disqualifier is disqualified regardless of intent strength. The check runs before scoring, not after it.
- **`lead.disqualification_requires_a_reason`** A verdict of disqualified without disqualify_reason is rejected. The reason is the only thing that stops the same lead being reworked at full cost next year.
- **`lead.stale_intent_is_not_intent`** Silence past three times the contact's own reply cadence, floored at twenty-one days, expires the intent claim. The lead moves to dormant and stops counting as pipeline; it does not become disqualified, because the person is still perfectly good and only the moment has passed.

- **`lead.one_open_lead_per_contact_and_account`** A second open lead against the same contact and account is a duplicate. Merge it before either is worked, or two reps run two cadences at one inbox and the account is lost rather than the deal.

## Actions

- **Route to an owner** (system) — Immediately. An unowned inboundlead loses most of its conversion value inside the first hour.
- **Send the first response** (agent) — Speed beats polish here by a margin that embarrasses most sequence design.
- **Run the disqualifier check** (system) — Before scoring,not after. Order is the whole point of the rule.
- **Reach a verdict** (human) — Pursue, nurture or disqualify. Continuingby default is not a verdict.
- **Move to nurture with a return date** (human) — A nurture withno date is a deletion with extra bookkeeping.
- **Disqualify with a reason** (human) — The cheapest action availableand the least used.
- **Convert to an Opportunity** (human) — Requires a scoped needand an agreed next step with a named buyer.
- **Merge a duplicate lead** (human) — Merge before working.Two cadences into one inbox costs the account, not the deal.

## Metrics

- **lead_to_opportunity_rate** (percent) — The honest funnel number. Rises whenthe intent bar is enforced, which is why it is unpopular.
- **time_to_first_response** (minutes) — Strongest controllable predictor of inboundconversion. Currently unmeasurable.
- **time_to_verdict** (days) — How long a lead sits in pending. A queue is a decisionnobody made.
- **disqualification_rate** (percent) — Near zero means the object is not doingits job, whatever the dashboard says.
- **conversion_by_source** (percent) — The widest-variance comparison in the funneland the first place to cut spend.
- **duplicate_rate** (percent) — Share of leads clustering to a contact that alreadyhad an open one.
- **false_conversion_rate** (percent) — Converted leads later lost with no purchaseprocess ever found. Calibrates the conversion bar.


## Examples

- **Downloaded a whitepaper, no reply to three emails** — Intent evidence exists and isweak and stale. A real lead, correctly ranked near the bottom — and the row most often re-scored upward at quarter end.
- **Referred by a customer into a perfect-fit account, no stated need** — Excellent fit,zero intent. This is a Contact and a target, not a lead. Calling it a lead is the first boundary blurred.
- **Asked for pricing and pushed back on it twice** — Strong lead. The push-back is evidenceof budget, not of its absence — the reading a mediocre seller gets exactly backwards.
- **Great discovery call, asked for a proposal, no other stakeholder named** — The classicmisclassification: converted to an Opportunity on enthusiasm. No named buyer and no agreed process means it is still a lead, and forecasting it is where the quarter goes wrong.
- **Champion from a won deal turns up at a new employer** — The highest-converting leadavailable and nothing watches for it. Today it surfaces only when their old address bounces, by which point a competitor has usually already called.

## Metadata

owner **Sales** · updated 2026-08-08 · review **unreviewed** · confidence **provisional**


> Eleven patterns: five executable, six blocked. The blocked six share one shape — intent is only visible once it is spoken in an email thread, so forms, pricing-page views and trial starts never reach the graph. The single highest-value gap is outbound.sent_at: the substrate records when the buyer replied and never when we did, so time-to-first-response — the strongest controllable predictor of inbound conversion, measured in minutes — cannot be computed, alerted on or learned from. It is available directly from the mail connector's own send log, which makes it the cheapest high-value ask in this file.
